title: Understanding Kingdom Law and Righteousness Part 1
paragraphs: Understanding the law of the kingdom and the right. Today I want to focus on a word that does not exist in democracy. It is the word of obedience. You do not obey the prime ministers. You do not obey presidents, but you obey kings. Jesus Christ is not a president. He is not the prime minister. You are not negotiating with him. Kings demand obedience. I am talking about the righteous kings. Today I want to focus on the power of obedience and commitment. Please write these two words. Obedience and commitment.

I mentioned something about success to you in our last session. I want to remind you quickly of those principles. I am convinced that every human being was created by God to be successful. Therefore, failure is an option. Secondly, I believe that success is predictable. This means that you can decide to be successful. Third, I am convinced that failure is also predictable. People fail because they make decisions that lead them to failure. They are violating fundamental laws.

Fourth, I am convinced that life is designed to be successful. God never created anything to fail. So if anything fails, it is because something in God's system must have been violated. God is more committed to your success than you are. Why? Because your success is good for his reputation. Anyone who makes a product that doesn't work feels embarrassed about that product, especially if their name is on it. Thus, God wants you to succeed for His own sake, not just for yours.

This means that your failure brings great sorrow to God. Therefore, success is built into the very core of creation. Success is actually automatic. The only difficulty is that you have to know its rules. The secret to success is understanding the laws of success. The term " law" is important, and I have come to the conclusion that laws are made to ensure success.

As we flew back yesterday from the beautiful city of Chattanooga, Tennessee, the pilots flew us to an altitude of 42,000 feet, one of the highest levels you can fly at. We were there for about an hour and a half. I noticed that the pilot was doing nothing but looking at the indicators. He had no control over anything with his hands. He was only looking at the measuring instruments. From time to time, he turns a small handle and touches something. That piqued my curiosity.

I wondered, how could this plane find its way to the Bahamas without the pilot guiding it? The captain told me that before you leave the ground, you get your coordinates, you get your frequency, and you obey the Federal Aviation Administration's rules. He said it is the Federal Aviation Administration that controls all flights over the United States. All I do is enter the codes and then relax. The aircraft picks up direct signals based on the laws and turns on its own. I don't touch her. It turns on its own.

It captures the coordinates and laws built into the system and automatically takes the plane directly to the airport in the Bahamas. He says, "All we do is land it." I realized that success is built into the system, but you first need to know the coordinates and then submit to the Federal Aviation Administration. You do what the watchtower says. I'm sure there are pilots among us today; we have a few of them. Reverend Rowe had been a captain for years. He will tell you that there is one thing leaders do. They obey.

Am I right, Father Rowe? Big words that pilots need to learn. You never argue with the watchtower. If they say turn three degrees to the left, I think it's best to do so. Why? Because they see the whole picture. They can see that plane coming directly towards you, but you cannot see it. Obedience prevents conflict. When you comply with the rules, you put yourself in order. This is what I want to talk about regarding integrity.

The captain told me, "When you get your flight plan before leaving the ground, they give you the coordinates, which are numbers that you enter into a computer, and the computer determines your entire route based on the rules they give you through the Federal Aviation Administration to obey." He says: " Once you get the coordinates, they have 3,000 aircraft in the air at the same time and none of them collide." He said: " Because each one is placed in its own system."

There are planes flying above you all the time, and flying below you all the time. You never see it because it has to stay in its system. What causes a collision is if the aircraft does anything that changes its system and enters someone else's space, there is destruction. Therefore, the key to security in life is finding order. Success in life is a product of discipline. I would like to talk about the system. Please take notes here. First, the power of law and order.

Creation was designed to operate according to laws and maintain order. Laws maintain order. When we talk about a country that has order, you can't have order without laws. This leads me to the second point. Wherever there is disorder, there is an absence or violation of the law. Wherever there is disorder, there is an absence or violation of the laws. So if you see a country in turmoil, it is because there are people who are violating the laws of that country.

If there is a disturbance in your physical body, there is some law that you may be violating. If there is a disturbance in your financial life, there must be laws that you are violating or lack knowledge of. The Bible says: "My people are destroyed, not because of Satan, but because of lack of knowledge." I think the question is: knowing what? These are God's laws. This leads to the third point. Chaos always precedes destruction.

Anyone you see failing at anything, you can be sure that the reason can be traced back to some point where they violated some basic rules. You see a young man you knew in school walking down the street, completely lost due to drug use. If you trace his life, you will find a point where he started disobeying the law, and now we have a ruined life wandering the streets. If your marriage has fallen apart, it can be directly attributed to some kind of disturbance in that relationship.

Someone in that relationship violated basic laws relating to trust, commitment, loyalty, or fidelity. Someone violated something, and destruction resulted. This leads me to point four. Please write this down. The key to the system is the law. Order brings success. So, do you want to know what brings order? Order is a product of law. This leads to point five. The key to success in life is not just knowing the laws, but submitting to and obeying the law. If I never teach you anything else, let it be this one.

If you want to be successful in God’s creation and in God’s kingdom, these important principles are essential. You must submit to the law and obey the laws, and God will grant you success. Anyone, anywhere in the world, who violates this basic principle can expect destruction. The law is not optional. it is necessary. But you must abide by the law to be protected by it. Laws never destroy, they protect. Breaking the law is self-destructive. This leads me to point six. Disobedience produces disorder.

Say that with me. Disobedience breeds chaos. Say it again. Disobedience breeds chaos. Wherever there are any signs of disorder, there is disobedience. When you disobey the law, you create chaos that causes destruction. Can you imagine a pilot flying the plane you are on deciding to create his own frequency? He decides to fly at his own altitude. I think life is simpler than we think. We hold them to impress others. If you obey the law, you are wise.

And I say to all of you here, and to the millions of viewers of this program via videos around the world on YouTube, that the success of your life depends solely on the rules you abide by. Disobedience guarantees chaos, and chaos guarantees conflict. Your life is falling apart and collapsing. So please consider what I am about to say in this next section. The priority of the law, as you know, God's purpose and plan are very simple. God's desire was to colonize the earth with the nation of Heaven.

God wanted to fill the earth with the lands of heaven. In other words, the nation of God is called the Kingdom of Heaven. His main goal was to transfer and establish his heavenly kingdom on Earth as a state. In Matthew 4:17, Jesus declared God’s plan. He said, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near to earth." Let everyone say: "Kingdom". The kingdom is a state. Now, why is this important? What I am about to say will be crucial to your understanding as someone who lives in a particular country.

I will show you how easy it is to destroy or protect your country. It's very simple. I will explain to you all the problems that our country is facing now. I will provide you with the solution to that as well. The reason for the collapse of nations is that those nations violated fundamental principles. And that is what God willed to do. If you want to build a nation, you must accept the fact that all nations are built on law.

So when Jesus said he wanted to bring the kingdom of God to earth, he basically meant that he wanted to restore heavenly laws to earth because nations are built on law. In Matthew 6:10 it says, “ Our Father in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done.” Where? On earth. How? As in heaven. I’m going to give you a list to write down. Six things to write down. I call this the National Order. The National Order. First of all, all nations are built on law. Write that down.

Nations depend on law to maintain national order. Laws are the heart of a nation. Laws are the skeleton of a nation. Your body is held up by your skeleton. Your bones. That’s what keeps you upright, your skeleton. Your bones. The skeleton of a nation is the law. If you take away the law, the nation collapses. So please write this down. First, these points aren’t on the board. First, the law guarantees national safety. National safety.

The reason you have bars on your windows right now and five locks on your front door is because you do n’t feel nationally safe. Why? Because there are citizens who break the law. Second, the law guarantees national security. National security. Write that down. Laws guarantee national security because when People obey the law, and you feel safe nationally. Not just as a society, but internationally. Investors choose countries to invest in where they feel safe.

Not just personally as human beings, but also where they feel their money is safe. For example, if you have a $10 million investment you want to make in a country, the first thing you want to know is whether the government leaders won't be tempted to take bribes. Why? Because violating the integrity law—bribery. So people start withholding their money because you're violating the simple integrity law regarding people's money.

One of the reasons investors come to the Bahamas is because we haven't become completely corrupt in our political system yet. I know there's a smile on people's faces. That's why we should pray that people in power actually have money before they take office. Hallelujah! Because when you're desperate, the temptations of compromise arise.

If investors don't feel that you respect the laws—just the laws of a decent agreement—if you agree to certain things and make them legal, then stick to your agreement, and then I'll give you my money to manage. So, the laws protect. National security. Third, laws guarantee national prosperity. What did I say? Nations prosper because of laws. If people obey the laws, the nation will prosper, not just from foreign investment. Please listen to me.

I've met many locals in our community who started a business with good intentions, and in the first week of opening, they were robbed. Members of this church will tell you that they started a business on Monday, just opened it, and dedicated it. On Tuesday, they were robbed. Now, would that encourage that person to continue with the business? You see, laws can destroy prosperity because entrepreneurs become hesitant to try their ideas in that environment.

Now, if local people aren't safe, how can you invite investors from all over the world to come and invest their money in your community? Laws protect us and bring us prosperity. There are countries in the Caribbean right now whose economies are shattered. Not because they lack money, but because corruption is so high. People are afraid to put their money into the economy. Obeying the law attracts prosperity. So every time you stop at a red light, you are protecting our country.

Every time you don't steal what doesn't belong to you, you're protecting the entire country. In other words, it's a patriotic act, not a personal decision. So, obeying the laws is for the protection of the nation. And that brings me to point four. The law guarantees national development. The law guarantees what? National development. There are certain groups of people in the world known for corruption, and wherever they go, they find it difficult to convince people to invest with them.

And you, you may know some of these groups of people, and you know that your culture can become a culture of lawlessness, where people no longer trust you with their resources, and that actually makes you poor. You see, when you obey the law, it attracts development. We're all here in the Bahamas proud of the progress we've seen in our country over the last 10 or 15 years. We have foreigners who have invested billions of dollars in the Bahamas, and we sometimes take that for granted.

And I remember talking to the president of one of the big hotels here, who invited me to give a seminar for the staff because he said he wanted me to address petty theft. Theft. Pickpocketing. Yes. And that's a big word for it. Okay. And he said that He sat me down in his office first, closed the door, and said, "I want to tell you something." He told me terrifying stories and began listing the problems they were facing with people breaking the organization's fundamental rules and stealing resources, as he put it.

"Here are the numbers," he said. He told me, and showed me on paper, how much they had lost in revenue that year. "You know," he said, "we're not sure how long we can stay here, because if we can't make a profit every time, we'll eventually lose it. Then we have a real hard time deciding whether to stay. My point is this: if you break the law, you can drive development away from your country. If people know you respect the laws, they'll trust you with their resources.

I wonder if God is withholding from you now because He's watched you for 14, 15, or 20 years as you've been abusing the law. He gave you a hundred dollars, and you haven't returned a tenth of it. Do you know why God made tithing a law? Just to test you. He doesn't need your money. He wants to see if you can abide by it." Only 10%. And we keep saying to God, "Trust me." That's a ridiculous statement. I can trust myself with ten dollars this week. I can double it next week. God, you've been doubling it for ten years.

How can I trust you with a million when you can't manage ten? So, it's not about the amount, it's about the principle. Can you abide by one fundamental law? Laws bring development. They attract progress. And fifth, the law guarantees national pride. National pride. When people abide by the laws, a sense of pride enters their lives. I always want to proudly say that God lives in the Bahamas. And everything that implies. I want to say that when you come here, the people selling to you on the beach don't swear at you.

They abide by the laws of decency and respect for visitors. Fundamental laws. They don't raise prices because you're a foreigner. Fundamental laws. Laws of conscience. Laws of not spitting in a man's soup because he asked for it back because it did n't taste good, and not smiling now. I know that has happened. I'm talking about the people who work in the kitchen. Look, God is watching. Every secret is known, and He knows what He entrusts you with and what He does not.

And God will take things away from you if you break the law. Ladies and gentlemen, are you proud of your family? Are you proud of yourself? How did you abide by the law? How did you not take that thing you could have taken? Are we proud of ourselves as a people who consider ourselves honorable and upright? Are you known as a people who respect the law? Do we take pride in saying we are from the Bahamas, Jamaica, Haiti, or Barbados? Are we proud to say that? Or are you ashamed to say you are from a certain country?

Abiding by the law brings a sense of pride. And sixth, the law guarantees national wealth. Not just personal wealth in God's eyes, but national wealth. When you abide by the laws, you attract national wealth. People trust you with their wealth. You know, the Bahamas was known as one of the banking centers in the world, especially for offshore banks and credit companies.

They poured billions of dollars into it over the last 30 or 40 years because they somehow felt the environment here was safe thanks to the laws that were in place. It is applied. When you start breaking those laws, people begin to withdraw their wealth. Now, if humans do this, what do you think God will do? If you start breaking the laws, God begins to withdraw what He has given you. The Bible says, "He withholds no good from those who walk uprightly." This is the meaning of uprightness.

I tell you, my friends, that God wants us to keep the laws. So, when Adam fell, there is a very important point to note. Adam was simply disobedient to the law. Can you imagine that the fall of humanity was simply because one person disobeyed a law? The law destroyed the human race. The Bible says that by the disobedience of one person, not by the strategy of one person, not by the army of one person, by the disobedience of one person, death entered all of humanity.

In other words, disobedience to the law caused the fall of the entire human race. If disobedience to the law was the cause of the fall, what is the only way to fix and restore it? To restore the law. So Jesus Christ came to earth not to bring a religion. He came to restore the national law of a country that had been violated. He came to restore the laws of the Kingdom of Heaven to earth. This is the crux of the matter. The whole of it. This Bible is called God's Law. Not God's suggestions, not God's feelings.

These aren't just worships of God. They're called God's Laws. And we read this morning when that young man asked Jesus Christ, "How can I get eternal life, real life?" Christ said, " Keep the Laws." You know, he didn't tell him to " pray." We love to pray, don't we? You have a problem, pray. No, correct the Laws. You're disobeying. Oh God, my wife, she's giving me trouble. Really? Let's pray. No, you don't need to pray.

You need to discover which Laws you're not obeying at home, because her actions are a reflection of what you do or don't do. In other words, we love to pray when, in reality, we need to act. Ladies and gentlemen, you and I aren't here forever; people die every day. I'm not planning on dying right now, but there's a possibility, so please listen to what I'm saying. If you want to succeed in the next ten months, revisit God's Laws. Start aligning your life with God's Laws. In fact, here's what I wrote Last night.

Grace came to restore the Law, not replace it. Religious people have used grace to disobey the Law. We really think Jesus came to replace the Law with grace. That's why we fail while we sing its praises. We worship in our poverty. We worship in our pain and sickness. We worship in our distress and frustration because we think we have grace instead of the Law. But in case you think that, let me read what Jesus himself said about this.

Matthew 5:17, at the beginning of his ministry, which is our Bible text for this year, says, "Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law." Now, why did he have to say that? Because he knew we would think that. Don't forget those three words at the beginning: "Do not think." Because he knew we would later develop a theology that says the Law is bad. Don't submit to the Law. Don't fall under the Law. I mean, you start to fear the Law. And Christ said, " Now, before I begin, let me explain."

"I did not come to abolish the Law or the Prophets who spoke it." In other words, here's what he says. I'm a New Testament Christian. What he means by that is that the Old Testament prophets no longer apply to me. Wait a minute. I didn't come to abolish the Law or those who quoted from it. There's no such thing as a " New Testament believer only." There's a believer who believes in all of God's law. You know, I assure you of this. He says, "Truly I tell you," I didn't come to abolish the Law, but for what?

To fulfill the Law. Fulfilling means carrying out, confirming, breathing life back into it, and giving it meaning. Why? Truly I tell you. He says, I love this. Until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter of the Law will pass away. Do not abolish my laws. Ladies and gentlemen, I really want to assure you of this. When he said he came to fulfill, the Hebrew word he used is very beautiful. It has multiple meanings. I came to carry out, to explain. I came to rebuild. I came to clarify the Law.

Jesus Christ obeyed every Law he wrote. For your sake. He obeyed it himself. He loved his enemies. His closest friends were sinners. He forgave those who crucified him. What kind of law is this? The Bible says, "Love your enemies." Did he do that? Yes. "Do good to those who mistreat you." Did he do that? "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." The Lord says, "Give to the poor." Did he feed them? He fed five thousand of them free fish and bread.

It is very important to remember that he did not come to abolish the law. He came to uphold it. May I say this? Citizenship is the right to obey the laws. When you acquire the nationality of a country, they give you the responsibility to obey the laws of that country. This is why citizenship should not be taken lightly. You not only receive the benefits of citizenship, but you also bear its responsibilities. If you break the law, they remove you from society and put you in a place called prison. Why?

Because you violated the right to remain in society. Prisoners are simply people who have broken the law and, in doing so, deprive themselves of their rights. The right to remain within the community. They cannot benefit from being free. Whenever I think about the Law, I think about this man. His name is Moses. What a man! I wanted to remind you of the basics of this matter of grace. I presented this last week, and the Holy Spirit told me to present it to you again.

John 1:17 says, “For the law was given through Moses; but through whom did grace and truth come?” "Jesus Christ. Grace means power. Truth means the original meaning. Moses gave you the Law. I came to give you the power to keep it and restore its meaning. He says: I came to explain to you what Moses said, because I am the one who told Moses what to tell you. My laws haven't changed. So, we are not free from the Law. We are free to obey the Law. Grace comes to give us the power to obey.

You cannot obey God's Law without God's help. Therefore, God has provided grace for you to keep the Laws. Again, I will be defining the Law over the next two Sundays, because the Law is a very confusing word for most people due to our theological confusion. When I use the word Law, I am not referring to religious rituals. I am not talking about all those customs that people impose on you and place heavy burdens on you that Jesus was against.

I am talking about God's simple laws in nature, the spiritual laws of this world that you are supposed to obey. If you obey them, you will live and prosper. Can you imagine a pilot saying to a tower..." Observation: "I've been flying for 50 years now." I have surpassed you all. I am more experienced than you now. I know how to fly this plane. Without your help, I think you'd find a lot of conflict in the world. Sometimes we think that way about God.

You know, I've been walking with God so long now that I can walk without Him. God's laws never change. God's law is so paramount in Jesus' mind that He said these words: "Whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments" (Matthew 5:19), " whoever breaks the least of these laws and teaches others to do so, what will he be called? The least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever does and teaches these commandments and laws, what will he be called? Great in the kingdom of heaven.

For I tell you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of whom? The scribes and Pharisees," then you certainly won't enter the kingdom way of life, the kingdom life. Now, this last statement—we'll work on it in more detail later because I think you need to explain what it means. But this is profound. Let me just say it as a kind of introduction. The last statement means that unless the laws you follow go beyond the rituals of religion, like the Pharisees, you can't experience the kingdom life.

In other words, religion will never give you a kingdom life. The Kingdom. Trying to do all these rituals. And by the way, the Pharisees and scribes ended up with over 669 little laws they told you to follow, you can't even remember them. They were in a state of extreme slavery. I'm not talking about religion. I'm talking about a national life in a country called Heaven. He says, if you obey the law, you will be called great. And if you teach others to do it, you will be called great in the Kingdom of God.

I suppose "great" means that God will also take care of you because you are doing His will. Please take note of this. The only two things God has given man on His agenda, very simple priorities, are found in Matthew 6:33. Just two things that Christ said we should think about. First, seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and everything else. He says it comes to you automatically. Remember I told you success is automatic. Yes. He links spontaneity in life to two things: the Kingdom and righteousness.

That's the secret. That's the secret. He says, don't just enter the Kingdom, even though that's great. Ask for that first. But once you're in the country, he says, you now need righteousness. Don't just be a citizen. Although that's great, he said, " But you need righteousness." So the two things you should focus on for the rest of your life are these two things. That's what I live for now and until I die. Only two things I'm concerned about in life. That's it. Just two things. First, the Kingdom of God.

And second, righteousness. That's it. He said everything else will be added to you. This chapter came when they were talking about what? Food, clothes, a car, a house. They were worried about how they were going to live. And he says, "Look, stop worrying about these things." They only agreed on two things. The kingdom and righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.” Okay, let me give you this quickly before we wrap up here. Look at Matthew chapter 5, verse 6.

Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for what? Righteousness. Why? Because they will be satisfied with everything they need. Notice it says you should hunger for something you don't think about too much. Hunger for righteousness. Hunger means wanting it intensely, and you will be satisfied. Look at this verse. Matthew 5:10. It says, “Blessed are those who are what?” They are persecuted for righteousness' sake." Why? Because theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Now, two things are happening here.

He says, "Desire it, but when you desire it, you may create enemies for yourself." wow. Ladies and gentlemen, when you decide to be righteous, you will create opposition because the whole world goes with the flow in one direction. And you decide to turn around and swim against the current, and the pressure is normal. Are you following me? no. You must understand this. Persecution is not someone plotting to kill or destroy you. Persecution is normal because you're going in the opposite direction.

It's the tide that comes against you. So don't consider it strange when you are persecuted. Now, don't misunderstand me. I need to define persecution for some of you. Some of the things that cause us problems are not persecution. It's our stupidity. Persecution is a natural opposition to your obedience to God. I repeat, persecution is your natural opposition to your obedience to God. You are not looking for persecution. It happens automatically.

He says: “ Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” If you decide to live in the kingdom and be righteous, opposition is normal. Here's why. This is important here. First, he says: “ Seek first the kingdom of God.” The word Kingdom means striving for God’s government, God’s sovereignty, and God’s authority on earth. Seek God's will. It is implemented on the ground. Seek God's protection. Seek God's heavenly influence on earth. Seek God's guidance.

The request for the Kingdom of God is that list. Write that down. He says, "Ask for it first." Strive to be under God’s government, his authority, his sovereignty, his power, his will, and his administration. It is a country. Strive to live under the government of that country. Ask for it first. He says, “So the first commandment of Jesus Christ is to submit to God’s country—not a religion, but a country. Now, the second part is just as important as the first. Seek first the kingdom and its righteousness.

So I want to put this down very quickly. This is what I call priority number two. Priority number one is the kingdom. Priority number two is righteousness. Here’s the trick. What is righteousness? The word. You have to write quickly because we’re going to make you good students of this. I’ve done the research for you and taken the words straight from Hebrew and Greek so you can learn a little and no one can fool you. Okay.

The word righteousness has nothing to do with wearing a long dress, or putting a cross around your neck, or burning incense, or not wearing makeup, or not wearing lipstick, or not wearing jewelry. It has nothing to do with any of that. Let me show you what the word means. It simply means those who are upright, just, and righteous. This word actually means obeying God’s laws. Decaeus. The word also means uprightness. It means being righteous.

The Hebrew word is difficult to pronounce; I think in legal terms, it means—and I like this—obeying the legal system.” Wow. Now all the lawyers are sitting up straight, right? I know that right away because that's a word all lawyers had to learn when they went to school. Am I right, Brother Harley? Corpus, huh? He's a lawyer. Okay. When you go to law school, that's what you learn. You learn the legal "corpus." Now, "corpus" means the body of the law. The word " righteous" means conforming to the legal body.

It literally means being subject to the legal process. Jeremiah uses the word exactly as it was written in the Hebrew context. In other words, righteousness means when you are subject to a king's law and receive his justice. The word " justice" means rights. So when the king is satisfied that you keep his laws, he gives you your rights. Christ says, "Seek first the kingdom." Okay, you are subject to him. Then he says, "Now be righteous, and keep my laws, and whatever you need will be added to you."

I will ensure that you get what is rightfully yours without any effort. You were never supposed to struggle for your livelihood. But Adam did a terrible thing. We have to deal with thorns and thistles just to get bread. We have to sweat just to get bread. That's what the Bible says. Because The law was broken. And God sent Jesus Christ to be our righteousness, to bring us back into conformity with God's law so that we can receive the King's justice. The King's justice.

Do you know why we had such a negative experience with most periods of colonialism? Because the kings weren't righteous. What sets Jesus Christ apart from all other earthly kings is that He is known as the Righteous King. He is the King who aligns Himself with the body of God's law. And God is love. Which means that anything Christ does will never harm you. He is subject to love. He is under the authority of love. Everything He does, He does out of love.

The kingdoms we were subjected to, man, they went into some of our lands. They took our gold, our silver, our shillings and took them to their countries. They plundered the colonies. They kept people oppressed. They made them less than human. They made them slaves. Those weren't righteous kings. If they had been righteous, they would immediately have been under the rule of what? The body of God's law. And God's first law concerning mankind is that they were all created in My image.

How can you oppress God's image as a slave if you are Equal to you? Then the righteous king is what makes Jesus a good king to be under his rule. I prefer to submit to Jesus Christ rather than any other leader in the world because he is a just judge. Clap, everyone. That's a good way to clap. That's why we only follow Jesus. You can't trust anyone. They want something from them. But Christ came to give to you, not to take from you. Because God loved you so much, he gave himself up. He is the just judge.

The Bible says, "I know my plans for you." Plans not to harm or hurt you, but plans to make you prosper and reach your desired goal. What a good King to have us under his care! That's why we can trust this King. A few scriptures for you to write down. Ah. Before you do that, write this list down quickly. The word bar—I've gathered this from research. The word bar means uprightness. Uprightness. Now, what does uprightness mean? When I read about it in detail, it speaks of alignment.

It means being in the right position or standing properly with authority. Uprightness means you want to be upright again under some authority.
